title: A character with health
intro: Four steps, one script that grows. The robot gets health that can go down and up but never past its limits, and a report of how it is doing. The stage beside the editor shows the health bar and whatever the script prints.

steps.title: Give the robot health
steps.prompt: The robot needs two numbers: how much health it has now, and the most it can ever have. Declare a variable at the top of the script (a member variable) called `health` that starts at the number `100`, and another called `max_health`, also starting at the number `100`. Every function you write in the next steps will read and change these two.
steps.starter:
# The robot's health, and the most health it can have.
# Declare both member variables here.
hints: A member variable is declared at the top of the script, outside any function, with `var`.
`var health = 100` on one line and `var max_health = 100` on the next is all this step needs.

docs.name: var
docs.what: declares a variable; at the top of a script it is a member variable that every function can use

steps.title: Take a hit, never below zero
steps.prompt: Write `take_damage`, which takes one parameter, `amount`, and takes it away from `health`. Then guard the result: if health went below the number `0`, set it back to `0`. A robot at 10 health hit for 30 ends at 0, not at -20. The button beside the stage hits for `30`; the checks hit for other amounts too.
steps.starter:
var health = 100
var max_health = 100

# Write take_damage(amount) below.
hints: Start with the plain version: `health -= amount`. Then run the checks and read which one fails.
After the subtraction, an `if` can look at `health` and put it back to `0` when it went too far.

docs.name: if
docs.what: runs the indented lines only when the condition is true
takes away from a variable in place

steps.title: Heal, up to the limit
steps.prompt: Write `heal`, which takes `amount` and adds it to `health`, but never past `max_health`. A robot at 90 healed for 20 ends at 100, not 110. Use the same shape as take_damage: change the number, then an `if` that puts it back within the limit.
steps.starter:
var health = 100
var max_health = 100

func take_damage(amount):
	health -= amount
	if health < 0:
		health = 0

# Write heal(amount) below.

tests.name: Healing past the limit stops at 100

hints: `health += amount` first, then check the result against `max_health`.
`if health > max_health:` with `health = max_health` indented under it.

docs.what: adds to a variable in place
true when the left side is bigger than the right

steps.title: Report the state
steps.prompt: Last, let the robot say how it is doing. Write `report`, which prints the word `Alive` when `health` is above the number `0`, and otherwise prints `Down`. Use `if` and `else`: exactly one of the two lines prints each time report is called. The stage shows the last thing the script printed as its status line.

tests.name: At full health it prints Alive
Healed from 0 it is Alive again
Two reports, one before and one after falling

hints: `if health > 0:` prints one word; the `else:` under it prints the other.
`else:` sits at the same indentation as its `if`, and its own line is indented under it.
print("Alive") and print("Down"), with the quotes.

docs.name: if / else
docs.what: runs the first block when the condition is true, the else block when it is false

docs.name: print
docs.what: writes a line to the output

godot: Open Godot and make a new project called Robot Health.
Create a 2D scene. Rename the root node to Robot and attach a script to it.
At the top of the script declare `var health = 100` and `var max_health = 100`.
Copy your take_damage, heal and report functions into the script, under the two variables.
Write `func _ready():` and inside it call `take_damage(30)`, then `report()`.
Run the scene (F6) and look at the Output panel at the bottom: it says Alive.
Change the call to `take_damage(120)` and run again: the panel says Down, and health never went below 0.
Add a Label node as a child of Robot, and in report set `$Label.text = "Alive"` or `"Down"` beside each print, so the word shows in the game window too.
